title: Local vs. global marketing: strategies for success - KOTA

facts.fact: The KOTA article 'Local vs. global marketing: strategies for success' was published on September 16, 2024, by the author Emily.
The article defines local marketing as focusing on a geographically defined audience, honing in on the specific needs and wants of people within a region, city, or neighbourhood.
facts.quote: Local marketing focuses on reaching a geographically defined audience, honing in on the specific needs and wants of people within a region, city, or neighbourhood.

facts.fact: The article states that platforms such as Facebook, Instagram, and Google Ads allow campaigns to be focused on specific locations through geo-targeted ads.
facts.quote: Platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and Google Ads allow you to focus your campaigns on specific locations.

facts.fact: The article states that WeChat dominates in China and WhatsApp in parts of Europe, where other platforms may be used instead of Facebook, Instagram, and Google.
facts.quote: In some regions, other platforms dominate. For instance, WeChat in China or WhatsApp in parts of Europe.

facts.fact: The article cites McDonald's as an example of a company that adjusts its menu in different countries to suit regional tastes while maintaining its core brand identity.
facts.quote: McDonald’s adjusts its menu in different countries, offering items that cater to regional tastes while still maintaining its core brand identity.
